svg.aria-label: How to write ം: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ം
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ം (malayalam), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xxiv: movement 1 for ം, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-034.jpg>. Source note on variation: Moag's Table III (p. xxiv) draws it as one movement to the right of the dash that stands for the consonant; in Table II (p. xix) it is movement 9 of അം, after the eight movements of അ. The drawn line starts at the upper left of the ring and runs clockwise, ending with its arrowhead on the left side pointing up. Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. The direction is read from a small arrowhead in the scan, so it is stated with medium-low confidence, and other sources differ: an unlicensed tracing app (sabari596's Malayalam alphabet demo) draws the ring of അം from its top, anticlockwise, and the matching signs of other scripts (KanoAI's Gujarati anusvara, HP Labs India's Devanagari anusvara) mostly run anticlockwise. The ring is separate ink, so the pen lifts after the base to make it. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline of the sign on its own rather than to Moag's drawing; that outline prints an open ring, so the path circles the ring's own centre line.
